key_insight: DRIVE learns per-sample fine-tuning weights that balance retaining pretrained knowledge with adapting to a new task.
engineering_relevance: For mechanics-oriented AI models, DRIVE could help adapt pretrained models to new datasets when original training data is unavailable, though the abstract reports no solid-mechanics validation.
method: Decompose sample contributions into anti-forgetting and adaptation components using Shapley additivity.
Modulate contributions with covariance-based diversity and regularize weights using sample-characteristic priors.
Optimize weights through a unified differentiable objective.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical stability–plasticity and estimation-robustness guarantees, plus empirical gains in overall performance, convergence speed, and robustness, without naming datasets or giving numerical results.
watch_item: Assess contribution-estimation cost and sensitivity to prior choices before applying DRIVE to mechanics datasets.
paper_title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization
